prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary.

worlds.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother kept from 1858 to 1871; the notebooks are now in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. The scholars counted 212,000 words in the notebooks and 212,400 in the book, the extra being small words the mother skipped. Her "chickins" and "sumer" appear in standard spelling, and her breathless runs without a period are broken into sentences, so her quarrels with her husband read more evenly, every curse in place. A dozen entries sit under new dates, matching corrections she penciled in the margins years later.
worlds.explanation: The daughter standardized the mother's spelling, broke her run-on lines into sentences, restored skipped small words and fixed dates the mother herself had corrected, changing how the diary was written but not what it said: she "tidied" it. "Tightened" means made more concise, but the book has four hundred more words than the notebooks. "Softened" means toned down, but the quarrels read more evenly only because of the new punctuation, with every curse still in place. "Spliced" means joined in material from elsewhere, but the redated entries are the mother's own, moved according to her own penciled corrections.

tightened.why: Tightening makes a text more concise; the book is slightly longer than the notebooks.
tightened.surface_fit: Breaking breathless runs into sentences makes the diary read more briskly, which is what tightening a text does.
tightened.inference: the book has four hundred more words than the notebooks, all small words restored, so nothing was cut for concision; the change was to how the words were written, not how many

softened.why: Softening tones down harsh content; the quarrels read more evenly only because of the punctuation, and every curse remains.
softened.surface_fit: The quarrels read more evenly in print, and a daughter publishing her parents' fights in 1902 would be expected to tone them down.
softened.inference: the quarrels read more evenly because their run-on lines were broken into sentences, while every curse stayed, so their content was not muted

spliced.surface_fit: A dozen entries appear under different dates in the book, which looks like passages cut and joined into a new arrangement.
spliced.inference: the moved entries follow the mother's own penciled corrections, and the word counts leave no room for outside material, so the daughter fixed dates rather than joining anything in

worlds.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother kept from 1858 to 1871; the notebooks are now in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. In a few dozen entries, her curses at her husband become "my husband was tired today," and the winter she wrote of leaving him becomes "a hard winter," each new line standing where the old one stood. These entries are shorter in print and evenly punctuated. Everywhere else the book follows the notebooks line by line, her "chickins," "sumer" and run-on lines included, down to the weekly egg tallies.
worlds.explanation: Where the mother cursed her husband or wrote of leaving him, the book puts mild phrases in exactly those places and changes nothing else, so the daughter toned down the harsh passages: she "softened" the diary. "Tightened" means made more concise, but the book keeps even the weekly egg tallies and shortens only the quarrel entries. "Tidied" means cleaned up the writing, but outside the rewritten entries the misspellings and run-on lines are printed as written. "Spliced" means joined in material from elsewhere, but each new line simply takes the place of one the mother wrote.

worlds.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother kept from 1858 to 1871; the notebooks are now in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. For eleven of the fourteen years, entries carry sentences found nowhere in the notebooks, and the book runs a fifth longer. Each appears word for word in the mother's letters to her sister from the same weeks. The misspellings, "chickins" and "sumer" among them, are hers in both kinds of sentence, and where a letter told a quarrel with her husband more gently, the book prints both versions.
worlds.explanation: Sentences found nowhere in the notebooks turn up word for word in the mother's letters to her sister from the same weeks, set into the diary's entries, so the daughter joined material from a second source into the diary: she "spliced" it. "Tightened" means made more concise, but the book runs a fifth longer than the notebooks. "Tidied" means cleaned up the writing, but the misspellings are the mother's own in both kinds of sentence. "Softened" means toned down, but where a letter told a quarrel more gently, the book prints the harsher notebook version too.
